decisive_items: Reversible Effect on Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) Secondary to Retinal Vein Occlusion After Stopping Niacin Therapy
severe macular changes with associated edema
persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 [79.3] μm over 12 visits
response.rationale: The figure title explicitly identifies the condition as CME secondary to retinal vein occlusion, with niacin therapy as a reversible modifying factor rather than the primary cause. R3 is the most specific and complete diagnosis.

rejected.why: Niacin-induced maculopathy is not the primary diagnosis; niacin is mentioned only as a therapy whose cessation had a reversible effect on CME secondary to RVO.
Cystoid macular edema is the observed manifestation but lacks the underlying etiology specified in the figure title.
Retinal vein occlusion is the underlying cause but is incomplete without the CME component that defines the presented clinical picture.
